description:
Programme or Project Overview

Utrecht University invites applications for a PhD position in art-science-action integration and challenge-based sustainability education. The project studies how creative and artistic practices can be integrated with scientific learning and real-world action in sustainability education, and how such integration changes students' engagement with complex environmental problems.

The doctoral candidate will work in educational design research, developing and studying teaching approaches that combine art, science and action across higher-education and community settings. The position connects the university's sustainability-education initiatives with its education-research community, and the appointment is a salaried four-year track under the CAO-NU collective agreement.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in education, sustainability science, the arts or an interdisciplinary programme, and show affinity with both creative practice and empirical education research. Experience with qualitative research methods and design-based research is an advantage. The working language is English, and the supervisory team spans education research and sustainability studies.

Highlights

  • Art-science integration in sustainability education
  • Challenge-based learning design
  • Educational design research methods
  • Student engagement with complex environmental problems
  • Higher-education and community learning settings
  • Salaried four-year PhD under the CAO-NU agreement

About Utrecht University

Utrecht University is a leading Dutch research university, consistently ranked among the top institutions in Europe. Its research and teaching span four faculties and a broad range of strategic themes, including sustainability, dynamics of youth, institutions for open societies and life sciences. PhD candidates and postdocs in the Netherlands are salaried staff members with full employment benefits under the CAO-NU collective agreement, so advertised positions are fully funded. Academic and support vacancies are published on the university's working-at portal, with clear deadlines and application instructions per position.
